evidence.exact_quote: - Shell injections in preview mode execute the shell command only subject to bash permission.

items.impact: A command labeled dry-run can still mutate files, network state, or external systems because bash permission alone does not define sandboxing, side-effect limits, timeout, cancellation, or rollback.
items.statement: CS-035 prohibits run execution and agent submission but explicitly permits shell execution without specifying isolation or recovery semantics for shell side effects.
items.title: Dry-run shell execution lacks a side-effect boundary

evidence.exact_quote: - No new shortcut behavior is inferred from this heading-only span.

items.impact: This prevents a heading-only migration artifact from silently becoming an implementation requirement.
items.statement: CS-036 explicitly limits the 6.3 heading to source lineage and defers shortcut behavior to its owning contracts.
items.title: Shortcut heading is correctly non-semantic

evidence.exact_quote: - Reserved commands include /new, /model, /effort, /mode, /export, /compact, /stop, /resume, /rewind, /revert, /share, /settings, /doctor, /help, /web, /skill, and /cancel.

items.impact: Consumers implementing the enumerated canonical set can omit later reserved commands such as /goal, /goal again, or /teach, producing inconsistent parsing and override enforcement.
items.statement: CS-037 calls its enumerated list the canonical reserved set, but later PlanUnits in the same document add reserved command behavior without reconciling this list.
items.title: Canonical reserved-command list is not extension-safe

evidence.exact_quote: - URL normalization applies and parse failure shows usage.

items.impact: Different entry surfaces can disagree about malformed URLs, schemes, redirects, local-network targets, or retry behavior, and tests have no exact error/result oracle.
items.statement: CS-038 requires normalization and usage on parse failure but does not define accepted URL forms, unsafe targets, canonical output, or offline/transport failure behavior.
items.title: Web parsing leaves URL and failure semantics discretionary

evidence.exact_quote: - override_builtin is /forbid for every reserved built-in slash command.

items.impact: The rule gives registry and runtime consumers an unambiguous authority boundary for reserved built-ins.
items.statement: CS-039 clearly forbids reserved built-in overrides and distinguishes rewind, revert, cancel, and removed clear semantics.
items.title: Reserved override authority is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - Deprecated aliases are shown distinctly from active commands.

items.impact: A color-only, icon-only, or untranslated distinction could technically satisfy the prose while remaining inaccessible or misleading.
items.statement: CS-040 requires deprecated aliases to look distinct but does not define accessible semantics, explanatory text, interaction behavior, or a testable visual-state contract.
items.title: Deprecated alias UI distinction is underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Expected events are tool.invoked when subtask: true, otherwise the canonical chat message event registered by the event owner.

items.impact: Non-subtask dispatch cannot be wired or acceptance-tested deterministically until a concrete registered event identity and payload contract are bound.
items.statement: CS-041 intentionally defers the non-subtask event name, but the resulting bridge contract has no concrete event oracle in this PlanUnit.
items.title: User-command bridge lacks a concrete non-subtask event

evidence.exact_quote: - Preconditions for each command remain preserved.

items.impact: Implementations can diverge on legal start, stop, pause, resume, breakpoint, step, evidence, and snapshot transitions, especially under concurrent commands or partial failure.
items.statement: CS-042 enumerates Debug Mode commands and says preconditions remain preserved, but provides no actual preconditions, payload/result schemas, invalid-state outcomes, or idempotency rules.
items.title: Debug UICommand family has no executable lifecycle contract

evidence.exact_quote: - OpenCode material does not override Puppet Master dispatch rules, storage paths, or reserved slash-command policy.

items.impact: External baseline material cannot silently acquire product authority.
items.statement: CS-043 establishes an explicit non-authoritative boundary around OpenCode reference material.
items.title: OpenCode reference authority is correctly bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - Custom commands can override built-in commands by name in the OpenCode baseline.

items.impact: The potentially unsafe upstream override behavior is documented as baseline comparison rather than Puppet Master policy.
items.statement: CS-044 records OpenCode behavior for comparison while CS-043 and its own negative constraint keep it non-authoritative.
items.title: OpenCode override behavior remains reference-only

evidence.exact_quote: - Capability discovery such as capabilities.get is a live provider/runtime contract, not a command-local cache.

items.impact: A capability can change or become unavailable between discovery and dispatch, and command consumers have no specified stale result, retry, fallback, or user-visible failure behavior.
items.statement: CS-045 correctly assigns capability discovery to the live provider/runtime owner but leaves commands without a contract for discovery failure or capability drift during invocation.
items.title: Live capability discovery has no command-side failure protocol

evidence.exact_quote: - Puppet Master provides a full Commands settings screen.

items.impact: A nominal screen can satisfy the acceptance text without usable create, edit, validation, conflict, loading, empty, error, keyboard, localization, or accessibility behavior.
items.statement: CS-046 asserts a full GUI management screen but does not define the minimum visible capabilities or testable states that make the screen full.
items.title: Commands settings GUI delta is existence-only

evidence.exact_quote: - AC-CMD01 remains covered: project-local commands MUST override global commands with the same name and resolution order MUST be deterministic.

items.impact: Concurrent create, rename, delete, or reload operations can observe different winners or partially applied states despite nominally deterministic static ordering.
items.statement: CS-047 requires deterministic project-over-global resolution but does not define atomicity, snapshot timing, or conflict recovery when command files change concurrently.
items.title: Deterministic override lacks mutation-time semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - If shell injection is denied, it MUST be blocked and an error substituted.

items.impact: Callers cannot distinguish permission denial from execution failure or partial expansion, and substituted text can accidentally be sent as ordinary prompt content without a typed failure signal.
items.statement: CS-048 requires an error substitution for denied shell or file operations but does not define the error shape, escaping, propagation, ledger event, abort policy, or partial-expansion cleanup.
items.title: Denied template operations have untyped substitution behavior

evidence.exact_quote: - AC-CMD09 remains covered: every User Command MUST appear in command palette and chat slash-command autocomplete unless unresolved.

items.impact: Commands may disappear without explanation, remain stale in one surface, or expose inconsistent disabled states, with no recovery route or accessibility oracle.
items.statement: CS-049 exempts unresolved commands from palette and autocomplete exposure but does not define unresolved, projection synchronization, visible reason codes, or repair behavior.
items.title: Unresolved command visibility is not a defined GUI state

evidence.exact_quote: span and must not re-own atomized source coverage.

items.impact: The retired bridge cannot compete with atomized PlanUnits for product authority or generate work.
items.statement: CS-001 is explicitly retired in place and prohibited from re-owning atomized coverage.
items.title: Retired bridge authority is closed

evidence.exact_quote: - There is one canonical Section 7 command-system anchor after cleanup.

items.impact: A cleanup can leave one heading yet choose a different anchor slug or break inbound references while still passing the stated oracle.
items.statement: CS-050 requires one canonical Section 7 anchor but does not name the canonical anchor identity, alias migration behavior, or an automated inbound-link validation oracle.
items.title: Section 7 recovery does not bind the surviving anchor

evidence.exact_quote: Commands_System reserves `/goal` and `/goal again` as Assistant Chat built-in slash commands. `/goal` resolves to `cmd.chat.goal.start`; `/goal again` resolves to `cmd.chat.goal.update`. User Commands and `override_builtin` cannot override these Goal Mode slash commands.

items.impact: Parsers or registries generated from CS-037 can accept overrides or reject built-in Goal commands even though CS-051 requires the opposite.
items.statement: CS-051 adds /goal and /goal again as reserved built-ins without updating the earlier PlanUnit that declares and enumerates the canonical reserved set.
items.title: Goal reservations conflict with the locked reserved-set list

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not define UICommand payload/result schemas in Commands_System.

items.impact: Builders cannot prove that every listed action uses the correct typed payload, result, stale guard, receipt, recovery route, and idempotency rule from the owner contract.
items.statement: CS-052 correctly refuses to re-own UICommand schemas, but it supplies no per-action command IDs or exact contract references that make its broad invocation list falsifiable.
items.title: Planning command delegation is not concretely bound

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not guess between one-off teaching and Teach capture when the user intent is ambiguous.

items.impact: Ambiguous help, implementation, teaching, and durable-memory intents can be routed inconsistently, silently change mode, or expose persistence risk without a deterministic user confirmation path.
items.statement: CS-053 states several negative constraints for ambiguous Teach invocation but does not define classification outcomes, confidence thresholds, clarification choices, cancellation, or localized and accessible feedback.
items.title: Teach invocation lacks a positive ambiguity-resolution contract

segments.summary: Reviewed CS-035 through CS-041 for preview safety, lineage-only shortcut scope, reserved-set governance, web parsing, override authority, catalog presentation, and the User Command dispatch bridge; found side-effect, set-coherence, URL-failure, GUI-oracle, and event-binding gaps.

Reviewed CS-042 through CS-048 for Debug Mode dispatch, external-reference boundaries, Puppet Master deltas, GUI scope, deterministic storage resolution, permissions, template processing, and subtasks; found lifecycle, capability-race, GUI, concurrency, and typed-error gaps while confirming OpenCode remains non-authoritative.

Reviewed CS-049, the retired CS-001 bridge, and CS-050 through CS-052 for GUI acceptance, migration authority, anchor recovery, Goal reservations, and Planning command delegation; found unresolved-visibility, anchor-identity, reserved-set, and contract-binding gaps.

Reviewed CS-053 and its adjacent repair lines for slash, help-icon, natural-language, context-carrying, Teacher-thread, memory-persistence, and discovery constraints; found no positive, testable ambiguity-resolution state machine.
